title.narrative: Project Votsira: improving maternal and child health in Fort Dauphin

description.narrative: Over 90% of the population in the Anosy region of Madagascar live in extreme poverty, with severe lack of access to health and education facilities. Women are particularly disadvantaged - the region suffers some of the highest levels of maternal and child mortality in the country, with around 20% of deaths in women aged 15-24 related to pregnancy or birth. Within Fort Dauphin, the urban centre of Anosy, sex work is a common form of income generation for women, and HIV infection rates in the town have increased by 64% in the last 4 years. Project Votsira aims to research the factors that affect women and children’s access to health services in Fort Dauphin, and to develop a series of well informed projects which will reduce maternal and child mortality. It will bring together members from all sectors of society in order to examine the cultural, social and economic factors affecting maternal and child health through interactive research activities including detailed case studies and focus groups. It will examine formal and informal support structures including traditional healers, and research in detail the choices available to women regarding their and their children’s health and the perceived risks and benefits of these.
